name: Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security
summary: A research centre at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (Baltimore) that works to prevent and prepare for pandemics and other biological catastrophes: biosecurity policy research and advocacy (DNA synthesis screening, AI and biosecurity), pandemic exercises, outbreak analytics for CDC and health departments (CORI), the journal Health Security, and training (the Emerging Leaders in Biosecurity fellowship). It is part of the university, so gifts go through Johns Hopkins; it publishes no accounts of its own.

spending.source: https://www.longtermwiki.com/sourcing/grant/-18Q_nYLfv (no accounts or budget of its own are published: our estimate from its published grants, Coefficient Giving $10M over three years from March 2023 and $3,908,161 over three years from September 2022 (about 71% of a year's share in 2025), CDC $23.5M over five years from 2023, Sentinel Bio $1,076,000 in November 2024 (over a judged 1.5 years), together about $9.7M in 2025, over our judged 70% share of its budget they make up)

lines.label: Biosecurity policy research, outbreak analytics (CORI) and training (every programme)
lines.source: https://www.longtermwiki.com/sourcing/grant/-18Q_nYLfv (the Center publishes no split of its spending; one line because charityevals models its policy research, CORI and training as branches of one catastrophic-risk model)
